en.title: Productivity gains remain concentrated as markets reassess the AI growth premium
en.deck: U.S. labour productivity rose 3.6% annualized in Q3, but total factor productivity increased in only seven of nineteen major industries in 2025. China's high-tech output expanded while fixed investment and goods consumption remained weak.
en.regime: Uneven productivity diffusion alongside concentrated AI investment and tighter financial conditions
en.key_risk: Capital deployment and valuations may advance faster than operating capacity, broad productivity gains and cash-flow realization, increasing sensitivity to financing costs and electricity constraints.

pt-BR.title: Ganhos de produtividade seguem concentrados enquanto o mercado reavalia o prêmio de crescimento da IA
pt-BR.deck: A produtividade do trabalho nos EUA cresceu 3,6% em taxa anualizada no terceiro trimestre, mas a produtividade total dos fatores aumentou em apenas sete de dezenove grandes setores em 2025. A produção chinesa de alta tecnologia avançou enquanto o investimento em ativos fixos e o consumo de bens permaneceram fracos.
pt-BR.regime: Difusão desigual da produtividade em paralelo a investimentos concentrados em IA e condições financeiras mais restritivas
pt-BR.key_risk: A implantação de capital e as avaliações de mercado podem avançar mais rapidamente do que a capacidade operacional, os ganhos amplos de produtividade e a realização de fluxo de caixa, elevando a sensibilidade aos custos de financiamento e às restrições de eletricidade.

signal_rationale.delta: The 20 November BLS release shows 2025 total factor productivity growth in only 7 of 19 major industries, while preliminary Q3 2026 nonfarm labour productivity rose 3.6% annualized. China’s October data show 17.6% growth in high-tech manufacturing alongside an 8.1% decline in fixed-asset investment during January–October; non-governmental fixed-asset investment fell 11.4%. This is a new productivity-diffusion test, distinct from the prior editions’ focus on equity repricing, European energy inflation and semiconductor valuation.
signal_rationale.evidence: BLS Total Factor Productivity for Major Industries 2025 (20 Nov); BLS Productivity and Costs Q3 2026 preliminary (5 Nov); Federal Reserve Governor Cook speech (20 Nov); China NBS October 2026 macro data (16 Nov); NBS Investment in Fixed Assets from January to October 2026 (17 Nov); ECB Financial Stability Review (Nov); Treasury TIC September (18 Nov); Japan CPI (20 Nov); European Commission flash confidence (20 Nov); Reuters market close (20 Nov); IEA Oil Market Report (13 Nov); Eurostat final October HICP release (18 Nov): 21.0% annual energy inflation, 1.89 percentage-point contribution and comparison with the 4 November flash estimate (20.8%).; NBS Industrial Producer Price Indexes in October 2026 (10 Nov), claim-specific fuel-and-power purchasing-price sub-index
signal_rationale.scale_path: AI data-centre projects move from announcements to financing, equipment delivery, construction, grid connection, utilization and adoption; productivity gains become broad only when operating firms change processes and outputs.
signal_rationale.transmission: Concentrated productivity gains and capital deployment affect valuations, electricity and equipment costs, credit underwriting, household purchasing power, cross-border flows and the ability of industrial sectors to convert investment into output.
signal_rationale.falsifier: Broader sectoral TFP gains, rising non-governmental fixed-asset investment and household demand in China, confirmed operating utilization of data centres and stable financing spreads would weaken the concentration-risk thesis; persistent narrow gains, project deferrals and tighter credit would strengthen it.

revision_reason: Revision 5 adds the claim-specific NBS Investment in Fixed Assets from January to October 2026 release as reference [17], separates it from the 16 November macro release [5], and corrects the 11.4% category to non-governmental investment in fixed assets in both editions and pending metadata. The four material corrections from revision 4 remain unchanged. The source audit is recomputed for 17 final references.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 22 Nov 2026 05:00 BRT; market observations refer to 20 Nov close and official releases retain their observation and release dates.
producer_checks.revision_scope: Corrected two additional material QA findings in both editions: added NBS reference [17], the claim-specific 17 November release for January–October fixed-asset investment (-8.1%), manufacturing investment (-2.9%), infrastructure investment (-5.1%) and non-governmental fixed-asset investment (-11.4%); and replaced the inaccurate 'private investment' label with the exact NBS statistical category. The 16 November macro release [5] remains the source for industrial production, retail sales, PMI and the supply-demand statement. The four revision-4 source, inventory, geographic-scope and conflict-attribution corrections remain intact. Existing charts and numerical series are unchanged.
producer_checks.source_vintage: NBS reference [5], National Economy October release, was published 16 November 2026 and remains the source for industrial production, high-tech manufacturing, retail sales, PMI and the strong-supply/weak-demand statement. NBS reference [16], Industrial Producer Price Indexes in October 2026, was published 10 November and reports fuel-and-power industrial input purchasing prices +18.6% year on year and +4.1% month on month. NBS reference [17], Investment in Fixed Assets from January to October 2026, was published 17 November and reports fixed-asset investment excluding rural households -8.1%, manufacturing investment -2.9%, infrastructure investment -5.1% and non-governmental investment in fixed assets -11.4% year on year. IEA Oil Market Report November 2026 was published 13 November and provides inventory composition, Gulf export and crude-flow comparisons, Europe-specific diesel observation and route-specific freight data. Reuters reference [9], distributed by Euronext and dated 20 November, attributes the late-session crude rise to concerns about possible attacks in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and pre-holiday buying. All cited source dates precede the 22 November 05:00 BRT cutoff.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: The NBS 18.6% y/y and 4.1% m/m input-price figures, the 17 November fixed-asset investment series and its non-governmental classification, IEA inventory components, Gulf export and crude-flow comparisons, Europe-only diesel price and route-specific freight qualifications, and Reuters conflict attribution are mirrored in EN/PT-BR. References [16] and [17] point to the same claim-specific NBS primary releases in both editions. Charts and numeric series remain unchanged.
producer_checks.visual_evidence: The revision does not alter the existing two charts, three evidence tables, one causal flow and one regional map. All chart values and structural visuals remain aligned across EN/PT-BR; the new source citation supports a text claim and does not introduce fabricated visual data.
